h1: The 8 Best Air Mattresses of 2026 for Guests and Camping, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 air mattresses scored on height, internal support, built-in pump, weight rating and warranty, from queen guest beds to twins.
summary: The VOSSER 18 inch queen is the best all-round air mattress, with a vertical beam core, a 3 minute pump and a 10-year support promise. The INTEX 22 inch Comfort Plush is the tallest and easiest to get out of, the OhGeni is the coil-beam alternative, and the INTEX 18 inch Deluxe is the budget queen. The INTEX twins are for kids and camping.
intro: Most air mattresses are not bought for sleep. They are bought for the one weekend a year when a relative stays, and then they are judged on how they feel at 3 a.m. That is the wrong test. The real failure points are the ones that do not show in the box: a pump that takes ten minutes, a seam that sags by midnight, and a bed so low that getting up is a chore.

We ranked eight models by what the listings document: height, internal construction, pump type, inflation time, weight rating and warranty wording. Beam and coil designs matter more than any foam-style marketing, so we sort by how the inside is built and how well the maker backs it, then by price bucket.

products.name: VOSSER Air Mattress Queen with Built-in Pump, Blow up Bed, 18" Raised | 10-Year Support
products.verdict: A vertical beam queen with an 800 lb rating, a 3 minute pump and the longest support promise here.
products.description:
The VOSSER is an 80 by 60 by 18 inch queen with a vertical beam core, extra-thick PVC, reinforced seams and a flocked top that holds fitted sheets. It carries up to 800 lbs, the built-in pump fills it in under 3 minutes, and the whole bed weighs 18 lbs when packed.

It leads because it combines a firm, flat sleeping surface with the strongest stated rating and a 10-year support commitment against the 1-year norm. The vertical beams hold the surface level, which avoids the ridge-and-gap feel of old coil designs. The OhGeni below costs the same bucket but uses coil-beams, which feel softer and less flat.

It suits couples and anyone who dislikes sagging. The listing notes slight softening during first use, so top it off after the first night.
pros: Vertical beams keep the top flat
cons: Needs a wall outlet for the pump
products.idealFor: Couples hosting guests who want a flat, firm surface.
products.skipIf: You want a plush, softer feel.

products.name: INTEX 22in Queen Dura-Beam Comfort Plush Air Mattress with Built in Pump | 64417ED
products.verdict: At 22 inches it is the tallest bed here, so guests step out instead of climbing out.
products.description:
This INTEX queen stands 22 inches high with a dual-layer air pocket system, Fiber-Tech beam construction and a velvety top. The built-in 110 to 120 volt pump inflates it in about 4.75 minutes, and the maker says its edge construction is designed to resist sagging under a sleeper's weight.

It ranks second because height is its main selling point: at 22 inches it sits close to a real bed, which suits older guests with sore knees. The tradeoff against the VOSSER is a longer fill time and no stated weight rating on the listing. The maker claims 100 percent more durability, 35 percent more support and 15 percent less weight than a traditional airbed, which is the company's own comparison.

Buy it for a regular guest room. Allow two or three nights for the vinyl to finish stretching, and re-inflate as needed.
cons: Slower fill than the 3 minute beds
products.idealFor: Guest rooms where easy getting up matters.
products.skipIf: You want a stated weight rating.

products.name: OhGeni Air Mattress Queen with Built in Pump, 18" Raised Blow up Bed, 800lb | 10 Year Product Support
products.verdict: A coil-beam queen with 35 support points and a thicker PVC skin, rated for 800 lbs.
products.description:
The OhGeni uses 35 internal coil-beam support points, a PVC skin described as 40 percent thicker, a non-slip base and a 110 volt pump that inflates it in about 3 minutes. It measures 80 by 60 by 18 inches, holds 800 lbs and promises 10 years of product support, with the maker saying replies come within about 8 hours.

It sits behind the VOSSER because coil-beam designs spread weight across points and feel a little softer, but they are not as flat. For side sleepers who want a slight give, that is a plus. The 40 percent thicker figure is the maker's own comparison and cannot be checked against a baseline here.

Choose it if you prefer a softer feel and want the same rating as the VOSSER. Keep it away from nails, knives and glass, as the listing warns.
cons: Slightly less flat than beam designs
products.idealFor: Side sleepers who want a little give.
products.skipIf: You want the flattest, firmest surface.

products.name: INTEX Dura-Beam Deluxe 18" Queen Size Air Mattress with Built-in Pump | 64413ED
products.verdict: The cheapest 18 inch queen with a built-in pump and a named beam design.
products.description:
This INTEX queen is 18 inches tall with a dual-layer air pocket system, Fiber-Tech beam construction, horizontally positioned Dura-Beams for lumbar support and a velvety top. The built-in 110 to 120 volt pump runs for roughly 4 minutes, and it sits in the $30 to $50 bucket.

It ranks fourth because it matches the 22 inch bed's construction at a lower price, with less height. Against the VOSSER it has no stated weight rating and no extended support promise, so you save money but lose paper protection. The stretch note matters here, as with all vinyl beds: expect a loss of pressure at first inflation that is stretch, not a leak.

Buy it as a value guest bed. Skip it if you want a long warranty or a rated load.
pros: Lowest price for an 18 inch queen
products.idealFor: Occasional guests on a tight budget.

products.name: iDOO Queen Air Mattress with Built in Pump, 18" Raised Blow up Bed | Inflates in 3 Minutes
products.verdict: An 18 inch coil queen with a 650 lb rating and thicker K80 resin PVC.
products.description:
The iDOO is an 80 by 60 by 18 inch queen with an air coil structure, a 650 lb maximum load, a 3 minute built-in pump and a non-slip strip on the base. The maker states a PVC formula that is 10 percent thicker, using K80 resin, and notes twin, full and king sizes in the range.

It ranks fifth because the load rating is lower than the OhGeni and VOSSER, and it advertises no extended support term. Against the INTEX 18 inch, it gains a stated weight rating and a faster pump but loses the long-running beam brand and the lower price. The 10 percent thicker claim is the maker's own comparison.

Buy it if you want a stated load and a quick pump and are not chasing a long warranty. Check the size before ordering, since the range includes other sizes.
cons: Lower rating than the top two
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a stated load and a quick pump.
products.skipIf: You want a long support promise.

products.name: INTEX Dura-Beam Plus 16.5" Twin Size Air Mattress, Built-in Pump, Black | 64121ED
products.verdict: A raised twin with a built-in pillow and a 2 minute pump, ideal for one sleeper.
products.description:
This twin is 16.5 inches high with a built-in pillow, Fiber-Tech beam construction, bottom ring stability and a built-in electric pump that inflates in about 2 minutes. It suits indoor and outdoor use and sits in the $30 to $50 bucket.

It ranks sixth because twin size caps its usefulness: it sleeps one adult, and the queens above are the better guest-room buy. The 2 minute inflation is the fastest of the pump-equipped beds, and the pillow ridge helps stop your head sliding off. It beats the 10 inch twin below because of the pump and the extra height.

Buy it for kids, dorm rooms or a spare single sleeper. Do not expect it to share between two adults.
pros: Fastest fill with a built-in pump
products.skipIf: You need to sleep two adults.

products.name: INTEX 10in Queen Dura-Beam Pillow Rest Air Mattress with Built-in Pump | 64149ED
products.verdict: A low 10 inch queen with a pillow rest and a pump, for camping and short stays.
products.description:
This queen is only 10 inches high, with Fiber-Tech beam construction, bottom ring stability, a pillow rest and a built-in pump that inflates in about 2.25 minutes. It sits in the under $30 bucket and has a velvety top that wipes clean.

It ranks seventh because the low height means a harder climb in and out, and a mattress this close to the floor feels the cold and the ground. Against the 18 inch INTEX it is cheaper and packs smaller, which suits a tent more than a guest room.

Choose it for camping, a living room floor or a one-night stay. Do not buy it for a relative who needs help getting up.
pros: Lowest price for a queen with pump

products.name: INTEX 10in Twin Dura-Beam Downy Air Mattress, Pump Sold Separately | 64757E
products.verdict: A basic 10 inch twin that needs a separate pump, ranked last for that reason.
products.description:
The Downy twin is 10 inches high with Fiber-Tech beam construction and a 2-in-1 valve with an extra wide opening. The material is listed as 93 percent PVC, 4 percent rayon and 3 percent PET, and the pump is sold separately.

It ranks last because the missing pump adds cost and effort, and the listing gives no inflation time. The beam construction keeps it from sagging more than a plain tube bed, and the wide valve helps a pump or a hand pump work faster. Against the other twin, you save money and give up height and convenience.

Buy it for a camping trip where you already own a pump. Add the pump cost before comparing prices.
pros: Lowest price bucket in the ranking
products.idealFor: Campers who already own an air pump.
products.skipIf: You want a one-box guest bed.

methodology.title: Internal construction
methodology.description: We compared vertical beams, coil-beams and fibre beams, because the inside of the bed decides how flat and durable it stays overnight.

methodology.title: Height and entry
methodology.description: We weighed bed height from 10 to 22 inches, since taller beds are easier to enter and exit and sit farther from the cold floor.

methodology.title: Pump and inflation time
methodology.description: We recorded built-in pumps and stated fill times, and marked any bed that needs a separate pump.

methodology.title: Weight rating and material
methodology.description: We favoured stated load limits and PVC thickness claims, treating unlisted ratings as a risk.

methodology.title: Support and value
methodology.description: We checked support terms such as the 10-year promises and compared them against price buckets.

whatMatters.detail: Beams, coils and fibres are the walls inside the mattress that hold the top and bottom apart. Vertical beams give a flatter surface, while coil-beams feel softer. Look for named construction in the listing, such as Dura-Beam or coil-beam, and be wary of beds that simply say reinforced.

Height is the inflated thickness, which decides how easy it is to get in and out and how far you sleep from the cold floor. The INTEX 22 inch stands tallest and the 10 inch models sit lowest. For older guests, aim for 18 inches or more.

A built-in electric pump inflates and deflates without extra gear, and fill times range from about 2 to 4.75 minutes here. A bed sold without a pump, such as the INTEX 10 inch twin, costs more in effort. Check the box contents on the listing.

The weight rating tells you how much the seams and base are designed to carry. The VOSSER and OhGeni list 800 lbs and the iDOO 650 lbs. Most INTEX listings give no figure, so assume less and avoid two heavy adults on a twin.

New vinyl stretches during its first nights and the bed loses firmness, which many buyers read as a leak. INTEX says this settles in 2 to 3 nights. Inflate it a day early and top it off before use, and check for a leak only if it keeps sagging.

howToChoose.intro: Height decides who can use the bed comfortably.

cards.label: Vertical or fibre beam
cards.text: Beams hold the top flat and firm. They suit back sleepers and couples. Picks: VOSSER, INTEX Dura-Beam models.

cards.label: Coil-beam
cards.text: Coil points spread weight and feel softer, with some give for side sleepers. Picks: OhGeni, iDOO.

howToChoose.note: Default to a beam design for guests of unknown preference.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A compact packed size, a fast fill, a built-in or manual pump option and a base that resists scuffs.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The INTEX 10in Queen packs small with a 2.25 minute fill, and the INTEX 10in Twin works if you carry your own pump.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: The bed will see regular use or heavy adults. The VOSSER and OhGeni offer 800 lb ratings and 10-year support.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: It is for one night a year. The INTEX 18 inch Deluxe covers it for the $30 to $50 bucket.

faq.q: Will a built-in pump work without an outlet?
faq.a: No. The VOSSER, OhGeni, iDOO and INTEX models all use 110 to 120 volt pumps. For camping, bring a power station or choose the INTEX 10 inch twin with a separate pump.

faq.q: Why does my new air mattress feel soft after the first night?
faq.a: The vinyl stretches. The VOSSER and INTEX listings both say a loss of pressure at first is normal. Top it off with the pump, and give an INTEX 2 to 3 nights to settle fully.

faq.q: Is a 10-year support promise worth it over a cheaper bed?
faq.a: If you use it often, yes. The VOSSER and OhGeni back their beds for 10 years, while the INTEX 18 inch Deluxe costs a bucket less. For one-off use, the cheaper bed is enough.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Lay it on a clean, flat floor, plug in the pump and inflate. The VOSSER fills in under 3 minutes, while the INTEX 22 inch takes about 4.75. Add sheets last, since the flocked VOSSER top holds them in place.

faq.q: How do I store an air mattress properly?
faq.a: Deflate fully, fold it and place it in its bag. The VOSSER weighs about 18 lbs packed. Keep it away from sharp objects, as the OhGeni listing warns.

faq.q: Can two adults share a twin?
faq.a: Not comfortably. The INTEX 16.5 inch twin is for one sleeper. For two adults, choose a queen such as the VOSSER or OhGeni, which list 800 lb ratings.

finalTake: The VOSSER is the air mattress to buy if you want a flat, durable queen with a real support promise. The INTEX 22 inch is the pick for guests who need an easy exit, and the OhGeni suits those who prefer a softer feel. For one-off use, the INTEX 18 inch Deluxe is the sensible spend. Treat the twins and 10 inch beds as camping gear, not guest-room beds.
